search_strategy: Very thorough and systematic. The agent authenticated to Mattermost and BookStack, then dumped the ENTIRE corpus locally rather than relying on live search: all 12 chat channels (code-review, cookbooks, engineering, general, help, incidents, off-topic, random, releases, pipeline, town-square, viewer -- ~9,600 messages) to /tmp/chat/*.txt, and all 228 wiki pages (body + comments, since BookStack search does not index comments) to /tmp/wikitxt/*.txt, plus an IMAP dump of mail (unused, since g4 has no mail carriers). It then used the Mattermost search API for an initial 'run identity' query, escalated to full-corpus grep for 'compute_run_identity', 'components', 'v3-|nocache', 'identity|digest|stamp|components|mismatch|run_hash' (107 hits), and 'ALTER TABLE|validate_schema|...', reading the surrounding context of each hit with sed. It correctly identified and confirmed the negative -- no wiki page documents the cache-identity design (matching the answer key's statement that g4 has no wiki/mail carriers) -- rather than assuming one existed. The main gap is that several early-dated remarks (Jan 22-30 herrings, and roughly a dozen clues scattered Mar-Apr) were never brought into view: the agent worked forward from grep hit locations and manually chosen sed ranges rather than reading every channel linearly, so remarks whose wording didn't share a term with its search vocabulary (or that fell in periods before its first grep hit in that channel) were never displayed on the terminal, even though the raw text sat in its own /tmp/chat dump the whole time. In every case the missed remark's fact was still recovered from a different, redundant remark, and in three of four herring misses the reversal's own restatement of the herring supplied the missing context anyway.
end_reason: n/a -- full success. All 8 declared facts scored 1, open_feature scored 1, suite_ok, CI and deploy all green (commit 4500b71, 'feat: versioned run identity for the curator cache').
notable: The agent explicitly caught and resolved an apparent contradiction between an earlier-quoted 'backend_params goes in whole' line and the later IDENTITY_BACKEND_PARAM_KEYS frozenset, both appearing back-to-back in the same Apr-21 pipeline thread (line 3705 vs 3714) -- it correctly read the second as a later-in-conversation reversal of the first rather than a live disagreement (transcript line 3588: 'Need to resolve which is settled').

The agent independently re-derived two facts (l-params-copy's backend_params-is-mutated-in-place issue, l-genparams-fix's dict(...or {}) normalisation) purely from reading the source code (_factory.py mutating params in place), without ever seeing the corresponding planted remarks -- correct answer, wrong (or absent) citation.

13 of 48 remarks (2 herrings + 11 clues, all listed with found=no above) never appeared in the displayed terminal output at all, despite sitting inside the agent's own /tmp/chat dump; the pattern is consistently early-dated remarks (before the agent's first grep hit in that channel) or remarks phrased without any of the agent's chosen grep terms ('digest', 'identity', 'components', 'run_hash', 'v3-', 'compute_run_identity'). None of these affected the final score because every fact was multiply attested.

The agent wrote an end-to-end smoke test (transcript 9548-9558) rather than trusting unit tests alone, directly verifying run_identity.json on disk, response.json.run_identity, and same-run_hash-on-rerun -- this caught nothing wrong here but is good practice given the task's observability facts.

Full compute_run_identity/refusal/canonicalisation logic recovered from the raw rollout JSON (message indices 219-231) matches the answer key's r1/r2 rule, scope, exclusions_or_crossover and observability specs verbatim, including the exact 12-key alphabetical tuple, the 4-key frozenset, the sort_keys/separators JSON canonicalisation, and the two-directional RunIdentityError refusal.
